Q1: Iodine presents known hazards (Tier 1) for acute and chronic environmental impacts, inhalation, oral exposure, and organ/systemic toxicity based on GHS. It also shows expanded hazards (Tier 2) for carcinogenicity, mutagenicity, reproductive effects, and dermal/eye exposure based on broader scientific data. Endocrine disruption is data deficient (Tier 4).
Q2: Iodine does not currently appear on any Lists of Concern or Lists of Low Hazard.
Q3: Iodine is extensively characterized in the scientific literature with 141,000 references, and its molecular structure is well-defined. While it has a good number of toxicity records (58), it has not undergone the most rigorous EPA evaluations such as IRIS or PPRTV, suggesting some potential gaps in its comprehensive hazard characterization.
